SMTO-SKL-0108 — Microsoft's sign-in reply was incomplete

GUID: 9fea7cc3-f8f1-5954-82f3-c6ab47ef57fc
Slug: microsoft365-token-response-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • After you signed in, Microsoft's reply was missing information SMTO needs. SMTO didn't save the connection, so your Microsoft account isn't connected yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to connect your Microsoft 365 account again, and finish the sign-in within ten minutes. A fresh sign-in rules out a one-time problem with that particular reply from Microsoft.
  2. If it fails again, ask the person who manages SMTO to compare the Microsoft OAuth App entry in Parameter Store with the app registration in Microsoft. This error alone does not establish a repair you can safely make yourself, and a wrong client ID, app type or secret can make Microsoft's reply unusable.

What success looks like

  • The browser page says your account is connected and the Agent can list it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the app's client secret or any sign-in codes into the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • token_bundle rejected Microsoft's token endpoint response: malformed or missing tokens or scopes, no scope on the initial exchange, an expiry over ten years, or an AuthError other than a revoked refresh grant.

What this means

  • Token exchange returns malformed tokens/scopes, missing required initial scope, excessive expiry or an AuthError other than revoked refresh authorization. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Token exchange returns malformed tokens/scopes, missing required initial scope, excessive expiry or an AuthError other than revoked refresh authorization.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe response-shape and token-validation metadata without exposing token values.

How to fix it

  • Check the Microsoft OAuth App profile (client_id, client_type, client_secret for confidential apps, tenant) against the Entra registration, and look for a proxy altering token responses. Then call microsoft365.connect again; if it persists, report it with the error details.
  • Verify the OAuth app and supported token exchange response; restart consent after correcting the actual validation failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported token endpoint supplies a validated bounded bundle for the intended app.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
